item.title: UK retail media jumps 32% to £2bn in first half of 2026
item.description:
UK retail media spending rose 32% year-on-year to £2bn in the first six months of 2026, according to IAB UK’s Digital Adspend Study H1 2026. The growth outpaced the wider UK digital advertising market, which increased 13% to £21.2bn in the same period.
Video advertising climbed 18% to £5.1bn, while search remained the largest channel at £9.1bn after a 10% rise. Display advertising added 9% to reach £3.1bn, putting retail media ahead of gaming (£0.7bn), digital out‑of‑home (£0.5bn) and classified advertising (£0.5bn). The study also noted that 70% of advertisers cited economic uncertainty as a top challenge, with AI and automation (37%) and measurement (30%) following. Connected TV advertising via internet‑connected devices reached £1.7bn in H1 2026, up 22% year on year. Mediasense forecasts that UK digital advertising will grow 12% across 2026 to £45.2bn before moderating to 10.5% growth in 2027.
“Retail media’s 32% growth confirms that commerce data is no longer just a bottom-funnel targeting tool; it’s becoming a strategic layer across the whole customer journey,” Rob Ishag, UK country manager at TripleLift said.
Before this period, retail media was considered a fast‑growing niche, but the £2bn milestone shows it has become a major growth driver.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/retail-media-hits-2bn-as-uk-ad-spend-jumps-32-in-h1)

item.title: Six retailers named as finalists for 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
item.description:
John Lewis, Asda, Morrisons, H&M, Dunelm, and Waitrose were named finalists for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, with the ceremony set for Wednesday, 4th November. The organizers said they received a record number of entries for the 2026 awards.
The Bricks and Mortar Innovation shortlist includes pairs such as Dunelm with Enactor and Waitrose with SOLUM. Supply Chain Innovation features nominees like OneRail partnered with NVIDIA and THG Fulfil. Payments Innovation shortlist contains entries such as Edenred Payment Solutions with New Look and Justt with Madison Reed.
The 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards are sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027. The ceremony will take place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November, featuring a drinks reception, three-course meal, and an after‑party hosted by Aurie Styla.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/john-lewis-asda-morrisons-handm-dunelm-and-waitrose-among-2026-rtih-innovation-awards-finalists)

item.title: Christine Russo reports from Retail Club and Shoptalk Fall 2026
item.description:
Christine Russo reports from Retail Club and Shoptalk Fall 2026, noting Retail Club drew about 2,000 attendees this year. She also heard organisers expect more than 3,500 attendees at Shoptalk Fall in its third year and first Nashville edition. She surveyed over 50 attendees across both shows to gauge their impressions.
She observed that dense 1:1 meeting schedules pull participants off the main show floor, leaving the floor quieter and creating lulls in activity. Off‑premises vendor events are growing in size and number, further drawing people away from the hall. When sessions end, empty stages and dark voids with vacant chairs appear, resembling a party where the kitchen is full but the living room is empty. Russo suggests placing content on every stage throughout the day, even during meetups, to maintain intensity and keep attendees engaged.
Retail Club is in its second year, after a first year that brought roughly 500 attendees. Shoptalk Fall is entering its third year and is being held in Nashville for the first time. The organisers of Shoptalk anticipated more than 3,500 attendees for this edition.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/rtihs-american-correspondent-christine-russo-reports-from-retail-club-and-shoptalk-fall-2026)

item.title: Sainsbury’s names Sam Littlejohn, ex‑Amazon, as supply chain planning director
item.description:
Sainsbury’s has appointed Sam Littlejohn, formerly of Amazon, as its Director of Supply Chain Planning, noting he spent almost 11 years at the online retailer. It is rolling out RFID technology across about 400 TU clothing stores, aiming for completion by September. The 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony is set for Wednesday, 4th November at The HAC in Central London.
A pilot earlier this year demonstrated that RFID improved stock visibility, accelerated replenishment and enabled more efficient inventory management. The RTIH Innovation Awards have now closed for entries, with winners to be announced at the November ceremony. He noted that the ceremony marks the awards’ fifth year as a physical event, having grown from an initial gathering of 30 people to today’s record‑breaking attendance.
“This year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records,” Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH said.
The RFID roll‑out follows a trial conducted earlier this year in selected stores. Last year’s RTIH hall of fame inductees were unveiled at a sold‑out event on 16 October at The HAC, featuring a drinks reception, three‑course meal and an awards ceremony hosted by comedian Tiff Stevenson.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/sainsburys-raids-amazon-to-bring-in-sam-littlejohn-as-its-new-director-of-supply-chain-planning)

item.title: OAIC launches investigation into HeyCyan app maker Shenzhen Qingcheng
item.description:
Australia’s privacy regulator launched an investigation on Wednesday into Shenzhen Qingcheng Future Technology, maker of the HeyCyan smart glasses app sold through Big W Marketplace and Amazon. The OAIC said it had been monitoring smart‑glass rollout since early 2026 and, in August, received a request from the Attorney‑General to examine privacy implications. The regulator sought information from Meta, Kmart, Google and Shenzhen Qingcheng, but the China‑based firm did not respond.
The regulator asked manufacturers and distributors how the glasses record information, who can access that data and where it is stored. The move adds to growing scrutiny of camera‑equipped smart glasses in Australia, where the government said in September it was considering blocking their use in government workplaces over privacy and security concerns.
The OAIC said it had been monitoring the rollout of smart glasses since early 2026. In August it received a request from the Attorney‑General to examine the privacy implications of the devices.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/business/privacy-watchdog-probes-maker-of-smart-glasses-app-used-by-kmart-products-202610)

item.title: Apple blocks major ad tech firms in Safari via secret iOS 27 list
item.description:
Apple’s iOS 27 updates, released in mid‑September, began blocking major ad tech firms from tracking users in Safari. The initial list names The Trade Desk, LiveRamp, ID5, Permutive and Experian’s Audigent as blocked, while rivals such as Zeta’s LiveIntent, Lotame and Yahoo’s ConnectID remain unblocked. When a user opens Safari, the browser stops communicating with the blocked domains, preventing them from collecting data or serving ads.
Apple requires every browser installed on iPhone and iPad to use its WebKit engine, so Chrome, Firefox and others are subject to the same blocklist. The new WebKit code lets Apple add or remove companies from the list without waiting for a full iOS update, although the code has not yet shipped to users.
“What this will allow Apple to do is make this block list dynamic,” Rowena Lam, senior director of privacy and data at IAB Tech Lab and product lead for its Trusted Server initiative said.
Advertising Week New York, a four-day conference that draws nearly 20,000 of adland’s finest, is renowned for on-stage programming tinged with optimism and creator reps angling for their 15 minutes in the spotlight. However, out in the snaking lines outside the conference venue, nearby hotels and dive bars, the talk often circles back to Apple — the biggest brand/provider in the industry — which reopened its war with the digital ad industry just a week before.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media-buying/apples-secret-blocklist-is-the-talk-of-advertising-week-new-york-mostly-off-the-record)

item.title: Zara and Gap use luxury tactics to boost media impact and sales
item.description:
Zara and Gap are adopting luxury‑brand strategies such as designer partnerships to increase their media impact value, with Zara’s March 17 Galliano announcement delivering $8.3 million in MIV within 48 hours. Launchmetrics found that mass‑market brands employing premium tactics averaged twice the MIV of those that did not from January 2025 to June 2026.
Zara’s Bad Bunny Super Bowl look drove $19.9 million in MIV, according to Launchmetrics. GapStudio’s first full women’s collection, launched in April 2025, saw a $158 version of Anne Hathaway’s custom shirtdress sell out within hours. In the first half of 2026, 78 % of GapStudio’s MIV carried the theme ‘accessible elevation,’ while Zara’s Galliano announcement showed 62 % archival authority and 54 % premium elevation in its coverage.
“Longevity most often comes from what happens next [from the brand],” Alison Bringé, Launchmetrics’ chief marketing officer said.
“It brings brand awareness to a new generation,” Zac Posen, designer said.
Mass market brands have borrowed from luxury for decades, so the tactics themselves aren’t new, The wider Gap business is growing, too, in part through this designer association.
Source: Glossy (https://glossy.co/fashion/zara-gap-luxury-marketing-launchmetrics)

item.title: CPG brands face tariff‑financing mismatch after July U.S. tariff finalization
item.description:
In July, the U.S. Trade Representative set tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on goods from 60 trading partners, affecting nearly all U.S. imports. Founders of CPG brands earning $2 million to $20 million now see a working‑capital gap when tariffs shift after a retailer’s purchase order is locked. Retailers usually pay on 60‑ to 90‑day terms, leaving brands to finance the gap between co‑packer deposits and eventual receipt.
Brands often use short‑term debt or factoring that assumes steady costs, so a tariff rise mid‑cycle leaves them repaying debt based on the old price while absorbing the extra expense. Founders should model each order at current landed cost and again at 10%‑15% higher, then check whether their financing can absorb the swing without breaking cash flow.
Before the July tariff finalization, import‑dependent brands faced shifting duty rates that made cost forecasting difficult. The new fixed rates removed day‑to‑day volatility but still allow tariffs to be applied after a purchase order is priced.
Source: SupplyChainBrain (https://supplychainbrain.com/blogs/1-think-tank/post/44783-the-hidden-financing-risk-behind-the-new-tariff-environment)

item.title: Wayfair expands Klarna BNPL to offer 0% financing up to six months
item.description:
Wayfair and Klarna have expanded their buy now pay later partnership to give United States shoppers access to 0% APR financing for up to six months across Wayfair’s brand family. For Canadian shoppers, the deal marks the first time Klarna’s full suite of BNPL options is available at Wayfair, while shoppers can also pay in full or split purchases into interest‑free installments.
The 0% financing carries no interest and applies to purchases made through Wayfair, Joss & Main, AllModern, and Birch Lane. Shoppers in both countries can choose to pay the total amount at checkout, spread payments over several installments without interest, or finance larger orders over longer periods. The partnership renewal was announced by Klarna’s Chief Commercial Officer David Sykes and Wayfair’s Director Curtis Crawford.
“Wayfair's decision to renew and deepen this partnership speaks to the trust we've built together and the real demand we're seeing for flexible payments for considered home purchases,” David Sykes, Chief Commercial Officer at Klarna said.
“Klarna has been a trusted partner in helping our customers shop with confidence, and renewing this relationship was an easy decision,” Curtis Crawford, Director at Wayfair said.
The partnership expansion comes as the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards prepare to highlight payments innovation, with entries now closed and the ceremony set for 4 November at The HAC in Central London. Payments will be a key focus area at the awards, which celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast‑moving omnichannel world.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/wayfair-ramps-up-its-klarna-buy-now-pay-later-partnership-across-american-and-canadian-markets)

item.title: YEEP! hits 4,000 parcel lockers and prepares Generation 3 rollout
item.description:
YEEP! reported reaching 4,000 parcel locker locations across the UK in October 2026. It aims to expand to 5,000 lockers by the end of 2026.
All new lockers will use the Generation 3 specification from 2 November 2026. Existing units will be upgraded to Generation 3 by the end of Q1 2027. The lockers were developed with hardware partner kernTerminal and feature a bespoke operating system for network management.
“Reaching 4,000 locations is a big milestone for YEEP!, and the launch of Generation 3 gives us another reason to be excited about where the business is heading,” Jamie Dickinson, CEO said.
Before Jamie Dickinson became CEO in December 2025, YEEP! operated just over 2,250 parcel lockers. Since then the company has expanded to 4,000 locations and plans to reach 5,000 by the end of 2026.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/yeep-hits-4000-parcel-lockers-milestone-as-it-gears-up-to-roll-out-new-touchscreen-technology)

item.title: Suboo enters liquidation owing roughly $655,000
item.description:
Bondi‑founded fashion label Suboo collapsed into liquidation after a creditors meeting on October 1, reportedly owing about $655,000. It owes Shopify $140,232.89 and Wayflyer $105,162.50, among other debts.
The company also owes DHL $60,909.41, FedEx $58,299.49, Swell Ltd $51,840.66 and Dongguan P&J Clothing Co $18,253.25.; Founder Sue Di Chio began work on the brand in 2008, and Christopher Darin of Worrells was appointed sole liquidator per an ASIC notice.
Suboo stocks its products in stores such as Farfetch, Bloomingdale’s and Saks and says it appears in over 300 premium boutiques across 17 countries.; The brand said it has fulfilled all customer orders and maintains no unfulfilled purchases.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/sectors/fashion-accessories/celeb-favourite-suboo-enters-liquidation-owes-655000-202610)

item.title: California Governor Newsom Signs AB 1693 to Speed Storefront Permit Approvals
item.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed AB 1693 this week, granting retailers quicker access to permits for storefront improvements. Under the law, local building departments must review and approve or deny applications in 20 days or less.
Retailers making upgrades to existing buildings may hire qualified architects and engineers to certify that their plans meet structural and safety standards. The measure, sponsored by Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur, the California Retailers Association and WC3 Chambers of Commerce, a coalition of chambers in West Los Angeles, is part of a package that will take effect on January 1, 2027. Other legislation passed alongside AB 1693 includes the COMPETE Act, which provides novel protections against statewide monopolies, and AB 1679, which allows small businesses to open temporary pop-ups in empty retail locations and forego onerous permitting processes, as part of a broader set of small‑business bills. Newsom said the provision will make it easier and more attractive to do business statewide in California, according to the governor’s office.
“Retail is constantly changing, and brick-and-mortar businesses need to be able to change with it,” Rick Chavez Zbur, Assemblymember said.
“Retailers throughout California are vital contributors to their local economies, yet they continue to face lengthy local permitting processes across the state,” Rachel Michelin, President and CEO of the California Retailers Association said.
The measure also represents a feather in Newsom’s cap as he looks to entice California businesses to deepen their roots in the state.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/california-permits-storefront-improvements-newsom-ab1693-1239317427)

item.title: Shippers push for AI-capable 3PLs amid nearshoring surge and global disruptions
item.description:
According to the 2027 Third-Party Logistics Study released Tuesday, 74 percent of shippers report major or severe impacts from global conflicts and geopolitical disruptions. At the same time, 86 percent are increasing their use of outsourced logistics services while 74 percent are consolidating their 3PL partners, up from 50 percent in the prior year.
The study shows 93 percent of shippers deem AI important, very important or critical when choosing a 3PL, yet only 12 percent of providers say they are highly prepared to deliver AI-enabled operations. Nearshoring remains a priority, with 74 percent of shippers diversifying suppliers or sourcing regions and 73 percent raising safety stock or inventory buffers. Nike’s chief operating officer told employees the brand is shifting away from owning much of its fulfillment network and will focus more on local partnerships, reflecting the broader move toward regional sourcing.
“The preponderance of what we’ve been facing is a global reset in the geopolitical environment, supplemented by natural phenomena and, on top of that, a large driving force of global economic reset,” Mark Baxa, president and CEO of the Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals (CSCMP) said.
The research was produced by NTT DATA, Penske Logistics and the University of Tennessee’s Global Supply Chain Institute, with backing from the CSCMP. Anne Reinke of the Intermodal Association of North America pointed to a large increase in Mexico‑bound intermodal shipments. Bloomberg reported last week that Nike is pursuing a nearshoring strategy more aggressively than before.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/3pl-study-nike-nearshoring-ai-third-party-logistics-cscmp-penske-1239316246)

item.title: Fed and PYMNTS show stablecoin demand trails infrastructure growth
item.description:
Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and PYMNTS Intelligence reported that while 42% of middle-market firms have discussed or tested stablecoins, only 13% actually use them. The Cleveland Fed found that only 21 respondents said availability through a current financial provider would increase their interest in stablecoins. Among the eight Cleveland Fed respondents who are using or planning to use stablecoins, four said they would accept customer payments and four said they would pay suppliers.
PYMNTS Intelligence data shows that 88% of companies receiving stablecoins immediately convert them to U.S. dollars. These findings indicate that corporate curiosity about stablecoins outpaces actual deployment, highlighting a demand rather than supply issue. The Fed’s review of corporate disclosures found virtually no evidence that non‑financial, non‑crypto firms hold meaningful stablecoin balances on their balance sheets. The same Fed research showed that more respondents wanted proof that stablecoins were cheaper or more efficient, more time to watch adoption, or demand from customers or suppliers. All three that envisioned stablecoins serving a treasury function also intended to use them for payments.
Over the past year and a half, stablecoins have secured clearer regulation, gained more institutional backing, and seen improved infrastructure from banks, FinTechs and payment providers, yet adoption remains low.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/blockchain/2026/the-fed-and-pymnts-intelligence-agree-stablecoins-have-a-demand-problem)

item.title: New York Fed says global supply chain pressure index hits 1.28, four‑month high
item.description:
The New York Federal Reserve reported that its Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI) rose to 1.28 in September. The index was up from an upwardly revised 1.20 in August, which itself had been raised from an initial reading of 1.06.
The GSCPI gauges global supply chain conditions by integrating transportation cost data and manufacturing indicators, and the New York Fed has published it since 1997. A reading of zero indicates the index is at its long‑term average, while positive values signal higher pressure and negative values signal lower pressure. The index reached a recent peak of 1.81 in May and an all‑time high of 4.43 in December 2021. In July, Reuters noted that supply chain pressures had started to ease after a four‑year high earlier in the year, attributing the earlier spike to the U.S.–Iran conflict disrupting trade through the Strait of Hormuz. The index is calculated as standard deviations from an average value, according to a graph included in the index. The last time the GSCPI had a negative value, or lower‑than‑average global supply chain pressure, was November 2025, with the current estimate for that month at -0.21.
In September, Bloomberg reported that the Port of Los Angeles blocked more than 120 million cyberattacks during August, with its cybersecurity team identifying intrusion, network exploitation, credential harvesting and malware attacks. The port is described as America’s busiest container hub for global trade.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/supply-chain/2026/new-york-federal-reserve-reports-global-supply-chain-pressures-reach-4-month-high)

item.title: Retailers reshape associate roles as AI shifts in-store expectations
item.description:
Retailers are training store associates to confirm or suggest product additions in under a minute as shoppers arrive with AI-driven research. Shoppers often spend a couple hours or more researching products via AI before entering stores, raising expectations for associate expertise.
Training focuses on product knowledge that exceeds what generic AI tools can provide, especially for complex or expensive items. At big-box chains like Walmart, many shoppers prefer minimal associate interaction unless a problem arises, while specialty retailers rely on associates as trusted experts. Associates receive AI-based onboarding help, but brands must ensure they can answer questions quickly without external tools.
“Back then, store associates were saying, 'Customers come in, and they've already done all this research, and they know more about the products than I do because they have access to all this information that I don't have access to,',” Nikki Baird, vice president of strategy and product at Aptos Retail said.
“AI will only return answers for what you ask it,” Garry Heon, senior vice president and sector head of retail and consumer goods, communications, media and entertainment at QualityAI said.
Before AI, the spread of branded websites gave customers product information online, changing how associates interacted with shoppers in store.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/where-do-associates-fit-in-an-ai-world-retail/831640)

item.title: Autonomous trucks log 440,000 driverless miles on Sun Belt routes
item.description:
Aurora reported that its driverless trucks had logged close to 440,000 miles by the end of June 2025. It now operates on 10 driverless routes across the Sun Belt, including a roughly 1,000‑mile Fort Worth‑to‑Phoenix lane, and expects more than 200 driverless trucks in service by year‑end.
Kodiak had 35 driverless-powered trucks running in the Permian by the end of June, with over 40,000 cumulative hours of paid driverless operations. Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Waabi began hauling freight for Warp’s LTL network on the Dallas‑Houston corridor with an observer still in the seat, and Waabi said driverless runs on Volvo’s purpose‑built truck will start next year. Waabi also said it has cut the time to open a new lane from three months to three weeks to, on at least one lane, nothing at all. All deployments remain limited to highway middle‑mile moves in good weather, leaving dock work, yard maneuvers, breakdowns and customer‑side tasks to human drivers.
Prior to June 2025, Aurora had logged more than 250,000 driverless miles by January after launching commercial operations on the Dallas‑Houston corridor in April 2025. Kodiak had already placed 20 driverless trucks in the Permian at the end of the previous year and grew that fleet to 35 by June.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/the-autonomous-trucks-are-coming-for-the-lane-not-necessarily-for-your-business)

item.title: Moralve adopts Amazon’s Global Warehousing to cut shipments from 5 to 1
item.description:
Since its 2021 launch, Moralve has adopted Amazon’s Global Warehousing and Distribution to centralize inventory, cutting inbound shipments from 5 to 1. U.S. sales represent roughly 75% of Moralve’s revenue, prompting the brand to seek a simpler way to stock overseas markets.
Through GWD, Moralve stores goods in bulk near Chinese manufacturing hubs and can allocate inventory to the U.S., Canada, Germany, or the U.K. based on demand forecasts, enabling rapid replenishment as sales shift. The service replaced the need for three-to-five separate international shipments with one inbound flow and a single purchase order, reducing administrative overhead and freight costs. Inventory levels are visible in a dashboard, allowing Moralve to shift stock between markets as demand changes and helping the brand avoid overstocking or understocking in any single market. Lead times are also factored into replenishment planning, helping Moralve balance stock across regions.
“[Inventory] sits in China, and then depending on the demand and the forecast, you can maybe send more to U.S.A, send less to the U.K,” Mo Kuhail, co-founder and CEO said.
Before adopting GWD, Moralve faced fragmented supply chains that made small overseas shipments uneconomical for its suppliers. Amazon’s Global Warehousing and Distribution service, launched in 2025 and expanded with new capabilities in September, promised a centralized inventory pool reaching Canada and Germany by year‑end.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/why-one-brand-adopted-amazons-growing-inventory-replenishment-service/832260)

item.title: Target revives Simply Shabby Chic line, launching bedding Sunday at $20 start
item.description:
Target announced Tuesday that it is reintroducing the Simply Shabby Chic home collection, with an initial bedding and decor line set to appear in stores and online starting Sunday. A holiday-themed assortment will follow later this month, and items will start at $20, with most priced under $50.
The collection features floral prints and textures such as ruffles and eyelets, including comforters, quilts, duvets, sheets, shams, decorative pillows and throws. Simply Shabby Chic is an affordable offshoot of designer Rachel Ashwell’s Shabby Chic brand, which first appeared at Target in 2004. The relaunch aligns with Target’s broader merchandising overhaul, which has seen Cara Sylvester named chief merchandising officer and Isaac Mizrahi appointed creative director at large to guide product concepts and mentor the design team. Mara Sirhal said the return will please longtime fans while giving new shoppers a chance to discover the style for the first time. She also noted that the partnership reinforces Target’s goal to strengthen its merchandising authority in the home category through style, design and value.
“who have loved it for years, while giving a new generation the chance to discover it for the first time,” Mara Sirhal, senior vice president of home merchandising at Target said.
“This partnership builds on our commitment to strengthen our merchandising authority in Home with style, design and value at the center,” Mara Sirhal, senior vice president of home merchandising at Target said.
Since Michael Fiddelke became CEO in February, Target has overseen a merchandising overhaul that included naming Cara Sylvester chief merchandising officer and bringing in additional senior vice presidents. The company also appointed Isaac Mizrahi as creative director at large to advise on product concepts and mentor the design team.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/target-simply-shabby-chic-partnership-home-merchandise-overhaul/832229)

item.title: Lenders use alternative data to approve millions more borrowers
item.description:
Lenders are turning to bank‑transaction data, cash‑flow records and richer credit histories to approve loans for millions of U.S. adults who lack traditional scores. Recent underwriting shows that verified bank transactions can lift approvals by up to 8% for underserved segments, Affirm’s new model adds 3.4% more completed purchases, and Plaid’s LendScore delivers a 73% approval rate versus a 65% benchmark.
Roughly 25 million U.S. adults have insufficient recent credit activity to generate a usable score, according to the CFPB. About 35% of subprime consumers hold neither a credit nor a store card, compared with 12% of prime and 4% of super‑prime borrowers. Personify Financial reports that adding verified bank‑transaction data increased approvals by up to 8% among underserved consumers while keeping credit costs steady. Affirm’s latest transformer‑based underwriting model generated 3.4% more completed purchases at comparable risk by approving applicants its earlier system had declined. Plaid’s LendScore model posted a 73% approval rate versus 65% for a traditional benchmark at equivalent risk, and at the same approval rate it observed 41% lower risk. The Federal Reserve estimates that 32 million U.S. adults are unscoreable, including 7 million with no credit history and 25 million with thin files. PYMNTS Intelligence counts roughly 44 million U.S. adults as subprime, or 17% of consumers, with 55% living paycheck‑to‑paycheck and 19% using buy now, pay later services. For small‑business lenders, a survey of 350 executives found 57% citing inaccurate or incomplete business records as an underwriting obstacle, and microbusiness credit applications approved at a 77% rate versus 95% for large enterprises, with 19% rejected for insufficient information.

Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/loans/2026/lenders-find-creditworthy-borrowers-hiding-in-the-data)

item.title: Etsy pilots Class 8 electric trucks on Texas route to cut freight emissions
item.description:
Etsy is deploying Class 8 battery-electric trucks in Texas as part of a pilot program aimed at reaching net-zero emissions by 2040, according to environmental impact lead Sam Brundrett. Through the Green Market Activation coalition, Etsy will pay for Environmental Attribute Certificates that offset the higher cost of running electric trucks versus diesel.
The pilot, which includes Amazon, eBay, Green Worldwide Shipping, Meta and Google, now has 63 members and is scheduled to launch in early 2027. Nevoya has been selected as the carrier and plans to deploy new battery-electric trucks late this year and early 2027, using charging infrastructure being built with Greenlane Infrastructure on the Houston‑Dallas corridor. Etsy’s commitment under the four‑year GMA agreement is to purchase a defined volume of zero‑emission trucking certificates measured in tonne‑kilometers, not tied to specific marketplace shipments. By 2030, Etsy targets a 52% reduction in scope 3 emissions per dollar of gross profit relative to its 2020 baseline.
“By 2030, the company aims to lower its scope 3 emissions per dollar of gross profit by 52% from its 2020 baseline,” Sam Brundrett, environmental impact lead at Etsy said.
“The certificates help cover the additional cost of operating electric trucks compared with diesel trucks,” Sam Brundrett, environmental impact lead at Etsy said.
The pilot was initially announced in January and is done in partnership with the Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) and Smart Freight Centre. The coalition also includes Amazon, eBay, Green Worldwide Shipping, Meta, and most recently, Google. The GMA pilot is focused on the Houston‑Dallas route due to significant freight volumes moving in both directions between the two cities.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/how-etsy-is-pushing-freight-decarbonization/832159)

item.title: Uber buys ezCater for $2.3B to boost B2B food delivery
item.description:
Uber announced Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Boston-based ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash deal. EzCater generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the past year and averages orders above $400.
The all-cash transaction will combine ezCater’s workplace catering platform with Uber Eats and Uber for Business, giving businesses access to over 140,000 restaurants nationwide and tools to manage ordering and food spending. The deal gives Uber access to a large pool of higher‑value, scheduled deliveries from corporate meetings, employee meal programs and events, and provides another way to put commercial delivery volume through its existing network. Restaurants will gain access to larger orders and new customers, while Uber Eats couriers will have additional earning opportunities from catering deliveries. The acquisition is expected to close in the coming months, pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, and Erin Mitchell will lead customer onboarding for Uber Freight’s Transportation Management business.
“Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” Dara Khosrowshahi, CEO of Uber said.
“Transportation touches so much of a company’s business—from warehouse costs and service levels to its ability to grow,” Erin Mitchell, Senior Vice President of Implementation, Uber Freight said.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/uber-strikes-2-3b-deal-for-ezcater-as-freight-unit-adds-supply-chain-exec)

item.title: Giant Company launches GLP-1 store tours in six Pennsylvania locations
item.description:
The Giant Company is offering one-hour store tours in October at six Pennsylvania locations to help shoppers using GLP-1 medications choose foods rich in protein, fiber, and nutrients. About 11% of U.S. adults currently use GLP-1 medications for weight loss, according to Gallup data.
The tours kicked off on Tuesday and will include tips on preparing foods that pair well with GLP-1s, with participants receiving product samples. The company will also host online classes led by dietitians or pharmacists that cover healthy eating choices and strategies for managing medication side effects. Loyalty points will be awarded to encourage sign‑ups for the online classes.
Grocers have stepped up their efforts to meet the needs of GLP-1 users as the popular medications change grocery-buying patterns and impact sales. For example, Publix began distributing a brochure in June that directs people toward foods that support weight loss.
Source: Grocery Dive (https://grocerydive.com/news/the-giant-company-glp1-tours-weight-loss-grocery-supermarkets/832234)

item.title: Payments pros target 2027 conferences on AI, stablecoins, instant payments
item.description:
Payments professionals plan to attend key conferences in 2027, including Boston Fintech Week’s tenth edition, to discuss AI, stablecoins, and instant payments. The Instant Payments Summit is set for March in Atlanta, while Nacha’s Smarter Faster Payments will move to National Harbor, Maryland, outside Washington, D.C.
The Clearing House aims to extend its real-time payments (RTP) network across international borders by the first half of 2028. The Federal Reserve Board has proposed amending FedNow to let U.S. banks and credit unions use intermediaries for cross‑border transfers. Conference speakers will also address stablecoin regulation following the Federal Reserve’s recent proposed rules for stablecoin issuers.
“Nothing replaces the in-person connections and relationships built at conferences,” Lucas Timberlake, executive director of Fintech Sandbox said.
“In an industry where change moves as fast as the payments themselves, developing an effective payments strategy in isolation is increasingly difficult,” Stephanie Prebish, senior managing director of association services at Nacha said.
AI was already a hot topic at this year’s conferences, and it’s expected to gain momentum as a major theme at next year’s events as well. The Instant Payments Summit, scheduled for March in Atlanta, aims to home in on the future of U.S. money movement, including instant payments and stablecoins.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/payments-conferences-for-2027/832239)

item.title: Fintechs urge Congress to grant Federal Reserve payment access
item.description:
At a Sept. 25 panel, Ramp and Stripe urged lawmakers to grant nonbank firms direct access to Federal Reserve payment rails, citing Ramp’s $200 billion yearly corporate payment volume while noting that Stripe currently lacks a Federal Reserve master account. Ramp said about 90% of its transactions rely on the Fed ACH system, and warned that without direct access its payment costs could rise for businesses using its platform.
The bipartisan PACE bill, introduced in April by Rep. Young Kim, would let fintechs use Fedwire, FedNow, and FedACH under oversight from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. Although the bill has Republican and Democratic cosponsors, it lacks a Senate companion and faces slim prospects before the November midterm election. Under current rules, nonbank fintechs must obtain state-by-state money transmitter licenses to offer payments, a process the legislation aims to replace with a federal registration. The Federal Reserve is also reviewing its practices per a May executive order from President Trump to broaden fintech access to U.S. payment rails. The Financial Technology Association called the bill a priority for the next Congress, citing continued market demand for faster, cheaper payments.
“even though we settle lots of payments every day, and it would be really efficient and really safe for our users to be able to do so,” Jonah Crane, head of global regulatory and policy at Stripe said.
“We think that (the bill) would enable faster, cheaper payments for consumers and for the businesses that we serve,” Alissa Kratsios, Ramp’s head of global policy said.
Currently, many fintechs that are not banks must secure money transmitter licenses on a state‑by‑state basis to operate. The Federal Reserve is simultaneously working to accommodate an executive order signed by President Trump in May that directs the bank to review its practices with the aim of opening U.S. payment rails to more fintechs.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/fintechs-press-for-fed-access/832233)

item.title: Facebook tests Reels-first feed for selected users in India
item.description:
Meta has begun testing a video-first layout for Facebook in India that opens selected users straight into a full screen Reels player. The legacy chronological feed is now relegated to a secondary tab, though users can switch back or opt out of the video-first view.
When the app launches, participants see an immersive video player that plays Reels in a vertical format, with the option to scroll to the traditional feed via the tab. Meta reports that its family of apps, including Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp, has 3.58 billion daily active users and close to 4 billion monthly users worldwide. Of that total, India alone accounts for more than 1 billion users across the four platforms, making it Meta's largest single market.
“People are showing us they want more immersive, visual, video-forward experiences, and video is where conversations are happening, communities are forming, and even commerce is starting to take place,” Tom Alison, Facebook head said.
In July, Meta signaled its intention to test a Reels-first experience in India after Facebook head Tom Alison noted growing demand for immersive video forward content. Alison wrote that video is where conversations happen, communities form and commerce is beginning to take place, indicating the strategic shift toward entertainment-driven feeds.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/facebook-tests-reels-first-ux-in-india)

item.title: DRZZL secures Whole Foods Market listing for two olive oils
item.description:
DRZZL has secured its first retail listing with Whole Foods Market for its Kitchen and Table extra virgin olive oils. The launch will be followed in November by a takeover of Whole Foods Market High Street Kensington’s window under the COOK PROPERLY campaign to teach shoppers usage.
DRZZL’s Kitchen oil is intended for cooking and the Table oil for dressing, a distinction rooted in founder Natalia Rudin’s experience teaching her audience of more than 1.5 million people—built through kitchen‑based cooking content—when and why to use each type of olive oil.
Before seeking retail distribution, DRZZL grew from Natalia Rudin’s cooking audience of more than 1.5 million people. She described the brand as being born from something she saw repeatedly – people are told to buy good olive oil, but rarely taught which oil to use, when, or why.
Source: Grocery Gazette (https://grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/10/06/drzzl-whole-foods-market)

item.title: Transportation prices surge to 92.7 as capacity contracts further in September
item.description:
In September, the Logistics Managers’ Index reported transportation prices at 92.7, up 2.7 points from August, while transportation capacity fell to 34.4, down 5.6 points sequentially. The overall LMI rose to 70.2, up 3.6 points, marking its second‑highest reading in four and a half years.
Warehouse capacity dropped to 39.3, a 14.2‑point decline that pushed it into contraction territory, the fastest such drop since March 2022. Aggregate logistics costs, combining inventory, warehousing and transportation, reached 246.1, up 2.5 points from the prior month. The pricing index has stayed at 90 or above in five of the last six months, and capacity has signaled contraction for ten straight months.
The pricing index has logged readings of 90 or above in five of the past six months. The dataset has signaled contraction for 10 straight months. (June’s 71.1 reading was the highest level recorded over that period.)
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/transportation-prices-surge-as-capacity-tightens-further-in-september)

item.title: Flipkart says active seller base nears 1.4m after dropping fashion commissions
item.description:
Flipkart says its active seller base reached about 1.4 million after 15 months of zero commissions on fashion. The zero‑commission model, launched in November 2025 with a ₹1,000 price cap, now applies to every fashion item on the platform.
Flipkart says many sellers pass the commission savings on to shoppers or use them to list additional products. The number of unique SKUs that actually sell on Flipkart rose 33% compared with a year earlier. Amazon India says it added 300,000 sellers to surpass two million total sellers on its marketplace.
“credited the zero-commission model it introduced in November 2025, which started with a ₹1,000 price cap and now covers every fashion product,” Sakait Chaudhary, Flipkart’s head of softlines, grocery and marketplace said.
“many sellers pass the savings on to shoppers or use them to list more products,” Sakait Chaudhary, Flipkart’s head of softlines, grocery and marketplace said.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/flipkart-says-its-active-seller-base-nearly-doubled-to-about-1-4-million-in-15-months-after-it-dropped-commissions-on-fashion)

item.title: FedEx Orders 2,000 Electric Trucks From Harbinger in $300M Deal
item.description:
FedEx has ordered 2,000 medium-duty electric trucks from Harbinger Motors in a deal valued over $300 million. The trucks are set for delivery by the end of 2027 and are expected to save FedEx roughly $40 million per year in fuel costs.
The vehicles will be deployed in FedEx’s parcel operations across the United States and Canada. Harbinger estimates each truck will cut fuel expenses by about $20,000 annually compared with a diesel counterpart. Over their operating lives, the fleet is projected to avoid more than 1.7 million tons of CO2 emissions.
“Electrifying a fleet at this scale requires vehicles that can perform the work our robust operations demand while also delivering meaningful economic benefits,” Paul Melander said.
“Expanding our deployment of Harbinger vehicles gives us an opportunity to continue making progress toward our fleet electrification goals while reducing fuel and operating costs,” Paul Melander said.
Prior to this order, FedEx had participated in a $160 million Series C financing for Harbinger in November 2025 and had acquired 73 of the company’s electric trucks through an initial purchase of 53 vehicles followed by an additional 20.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/fedex-electric-trucks-evs-harbinger-300-million-diesel-fuel-costs-1239314389)

item.title: Plaid launches credit and fraud models, lifting loan repayment prediction 42%
item.description:
Plaid launched its new credit and fraud models on Tuesday, saying LendScore 2 improves loan repayment prediction by 42% over traditional data and that Instant Link enables real‑time cash‑flow sharing. The Instant Link model lets eligible consumers share cash‑flow insights with lenders in seconds, while a new AI foundation model aims to strengthen fraud detection by learning from patterns across the Plaid Network.
LendScore 2 uses cash‑flow underwriting and is said to predict repayment ability with 42% greater strength than traditional credit data alone. LendScore Arc, a transformer‑based model introduced Tuesday, learns from the order and timing of borrowers’ transactions and is described as Plaid’s best‑performing credit model yet. Specialized versions of the models are now available for auto, home and short‑term loans. Plaid’s sequential foundation model now powers its ACH risk product Protect to better predict payment risk.
“The next generation of LendScore and specialized models close that gap at scale, and with Arc, we’re giving lenders new tools to expand access to more affordable credit,” Michelle Young, Plaid Credit Product Lead said.
“They build on foundation models that already understand how financial behavior unfolds over time, across the Plaid Network, and that means better decisions, and better outcomes, for our customers and the millions of people who depend on those services to manage their own financial lives,” Will Robinson, Plaid Chief Technology Officer said.
In June, PYMNTS reported that lenders are shifting to models built around real‑time behavior, arguing that what a consumer earns and owes today matters more than their credit score from six months ago. The same PYMNTS Intelligence and Plaid collaboration found that 94% of surveyed firms are not yet fully compliance‑ready for new Nacha rules requiring active fraud monitoring on the ACH network. This gap has prompted Plaid to build models that turn cash‑flow data into actionable credit and
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/consumer-finance/2026/plaid-launches-credit-and-fraud-models-fueled-by-cash-flow-data)

item.title: Super El Niño forces retailers to rethink winter inventory
item.description:
The Super El Niño weather pattern is prompting retailers to reassess their winter merchandise plans as December approaches. Analysts warn that warm winter conditions could hurt sales of cold‑weather apparel and force companies like Deckers to discount Ugg footwear if December temperatures rise.
The phenomenon’s strongest effects are expected in North America during the fall and winter months, disrupting typical seasonal merchandising cycles. With inventory already locked‑in well in advance for the season, retailers face the risk of sales misses and excess stock if consumer demand fails to materialize. VF Corp.’s brands, including The North Face and Timberland, are cited as carrying significant risk from warmer weather patterns observed in the 2015 and 2023 El Niño cycles. Historical data shows that warm anomalies in critical winter months have consistently reduced consumer spending on coats and other softgoods.
“This could be potentially one of the top 10 warmest winters starting in the month of December, so some of the decision-making that can happen with retailers is they shift their inventory too early and move it to discount,” Matthew Porcelli, meteorologist and senior solutions engineer at The Weather Company said.
“Consumers don't buy coats when it is warm outside,” Ike Boruchow, Wells Fargo analyst said.
Just when merchandising and inventory management seemed complicated enough, thanks to shifting tariffs and rising costs, along comes the strongest El Niño weather disruption on record. Burlington because traditionally they have sold more coats and were hit hard by an El Niño a decade ago.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/what-the-super-el-nino-means-for-retail/831188)

item.title: Maverik selects NIQ for customer insights across its 830-plus stores
item.description:
Maverik has chosen NielsenIQ as its customer insights and analytics provider for its network of over 830 sites across 20 states. Under the agreement, Maverik and its suppliers will use NIQ’s Activate platform to view business performance in a single location.
The platform combines Maverik’s first‑party data with NIQ’s analytics and consumer intelligence offering.
“By selecting NIQ as our customer insights and analytics provider, we are establishing a standardised approach that gives suppliers access to Maverik’s point-of-sale and loyalty insights, helping them make informed decisions and identify opportunities for mutual growth,” Byron Williams, Maverik category and merchandising senior director said.
NIQ stated that the announcement broadens its retail collaboration presence in the convenience channel and reflects the increasing value of measuring and planning performance together.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/news/maverik-niq-customer-insights-analytics)

item.title: Hackers hijack ASOS app, push extortion message to thousands; stock drops 13%
item.description:
On Tuesday, hackers hijacked ASOS’s official app to send a push notification titled “ASOS HACKED” to thousands of customers, claiming they had compromised the retailer’s Snowflake environment and threatening to leak data. The incident caused ASOS’s share price to fall as much as 13% on the day of the attack.
The push notification was sent through ASOS’s official notification system and directed users to a Telegram channel linked to the Xuanye Group. ASOS told the BBC it is investigating the claims and said its website and app continued to operate normally. Snowflake, the cloud data platform referenced by the attackers, provides storage and analytics for large datasets. Cybersecurity experts note that sending push notifications usually requires access separate from a data environment, suggesting the breach may extend beyond Snowflake.
The incident is part of a broader series of cyberattacks affecting retailers worldwide. ASOS uses Snowflake to store and analyze large volumes of data.
Source: RetailDetail EU (https://retaildetail.eu/news/fashion/hackers-hijack-asos-app-to-post-extortion-message)

item.title: meCore launches AI platform with 300k-product catalog for personalized style
item.description:
meCore recently launched an AI-powered fashion platform that offers a catalog of over 300,000 products to deliver personalized style profiles. Abdollahian launched meCore with the idea that AI should support human individuality, not just group people into predictable categories, embodying the mission to “refuse to be beige.”
Users can build evolving aesthetic profiles, dubbed “Cores,” that shift as their tastes, moods and inspirations change. The service draws on an AI engine and a library of more than 300,000 items from stores including Bloomingdale’s, Saks Fifth Avenue, Neiman Marcus and Anthropologie to surface pieces from labels such as Khaite, Veronica Beard, Zimmermann and Rag & Bone. Shoppers can upload any image or photo to receive wardrobe suggestions that match their personal style.
“The idea for meCore came from a gap I kept seeing as AI became increasingly capable but still fell short of truly understanding who we are and what we want at any given moment,” Golnaz Abdollahian, founder of meCore said.
As consumers become weary of one‑size‑fits‑all product suggestions, meCore offers a more considered method of discovery through its personalized “Cores” profiles. Those profiles are designed to update continuously in line with each individual’s evolving preferences and inspirations.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/mecore-uses-ai-to-turn-vibes-into-personalized-style-1239310134)

item.title: FTC sends over $100,000 in refunds to 6,205 GOAT customers
item.description:
The Federal Trade Commission is distributing refund checks or PayPal payments to 6,205 consumers who were harmed by GOAT’s deceptive shipping and refund practices. The payments total more than $100,000, and most recipients must cash paper checks within 90 days.
The refunds stem from a 2024 FTC complaint alleging that GOAT failed to ship priority orders as promised and did not give buyers the option to accept a delay or cancel for a prompt refund. The complaint also said GOAT’s “Buyer Protection” policy lacked a system to honor refunds for inauthentic, incorrect or misdescribed items, often denying or only partially refunding claims. As part of a 2025 settlement, GOAT already returned more than $736,000 to affected customers. Consumers with questions can contact the refund administrator, JND Legal Administration, at 1-888-970-2410 or visit the FTC website for FAQs.
In 2024, the FTC filed a complaint accusing GOAT of violating its Mail, Internet or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule by not honoring shipping promises and refund options. In 2025, GOAT settled the case by directly refunding over $736,000 to customers before the FTC began issuing the current payments.
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-issues-redress-payments-consumers-impacted-goats-deceptive-shipping-refund-policies)

item.title: UK shoppers default to large retailers, missing savings, survey shows
item.description:
Idealo's survey of over 2,000 UK online shoppers found that 67% default to large online marketplaces or standard search engines out of habit. Although 91% of respondents research before buying and 84% of those compare prices, just 8% begin their search on a dedicated price comparison platform.
Nearly three-quarters (72%) of shoppers use price comparison sites mainly or only for expensive, considered purchases, while only 13% rely on them for everyday shopping. Trust in price comparison sites stands at 71%, far higher than the 31% trust in social media deals and influencer recommendations, with 37% actively distrusting influencer claims. Three-quarters (75%) of shoppers say they would find it easier to compare prices online for at least one product category, citing mobile phones (32%), electronics (31%) and groceries (30%) as top areas. Only 43% of shoppers trust that Black Friday discounts are genuine price reductions, with just 10% trusting them completely and 27% actively distrusting them. The team at shopping comparison site Idealo surveyed over 2,000 UK online shoppers to find out how people research and compare prices when shopping online.
“Rethinking how we start our online product research can completely transform household shopping budgets. By switching from default browsing habits to independent comparison, consumers spend less time searching and more money saving,” Katy Phillips, Senior Brand & Communications Manager, idealo said.
Source: ChannelX (https://channelx.world/2026/10/67-of-uk-shoppers-default-to-retail-giants-leaving-savings-on-the-table)

item.title: Belgian government proposes 0%, 9%, 22% VAT model, predicts higher grocery bills
item.description:
The Belgian federal government is considering a new VAT model that would set rates at 0%, 9%, and 22%. While basic food items would become cheaper under the 0% rate, the average supermarket shopper’s total bill is still expected to increase.
Under the proposal, basic food items would be taxed at 0%. Products currently taxed at 6% or 12% would shift to a 9% VAT rate. All other goods and services would be subject to the new standard rate of 22%. The government states the overhaul aims to generate billions of euros in extra budgetary flexibility. Negotiations over the VAT reform are still ongoing and have not been finalized. The reform is described as a comprehensive overhaul of Belgium's VAT system. While basic food items would become cheaper, snacks and other discretionary goods are expected to become more expensive. For the average supermarket shopper, the overall grocery bill is projected to increase despite lower prices on staples. The VAT reform remains a proposal and has not yet been enacted into law. No date has been set for when the new rates might take effect. The De Wever government cites budgetary needs as the primary motivation for the VAT overhaul. Retailers could see shifting demand as basic foods become cheaper and snacks more expensive. Consumers may alter their shopping baskets in response to the changing price incentives.
Source: RetailDetail EU (https://retaildetail.eu/news/food/belgian-vat-reform-threatens-to-make-groceries-more-expensive-despite-the-zero-rate)

item.title: Target posts 5.3% Q2 sales gain as holiday turnaround begins
item.description:
Target reported Q2 net sales up 5.3% year over year to $26.5 billion, with comparable sales rising 3.8% in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. This follows a 2025 holiday quarter in which net sales fell 1.5% and comparable sales dropped 3.9%.
In September, Target cut prices on apparel and home merchandise to attract value‑conscious shoppers. The retailer also expanded its online marketplace and revived its Beauty Studio experience after ending the Ulta partnership.
“For the holiday season, Target’s ability to combine value with inspiration — especially in an environment where price is important to consumers — will be something to nail during the holiday season,” Katherine Black, partner at Kearney leading food, drug and mass market retail said.
Target entered the 2025 holiday quarter after consecutive sales declines and faced staffing and store‑order challenges. Saunders said Target had a solid gift assortment and private‑label holiday food innovations, but described them as drops in an otherwise insipid ocean.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/target-retail-holiday-season-performance/831858)

item.title: 7-Eleven shuts all 31 stores in India by end of September 2026
item.description:
Seven & i Holdings confirmed that its master franchisee Reliance closed all 31 7-Eleven stores in Mumbai and Pune as of 30 September 2026. In the financial year to March 2026, the Indian operation posted revenue of about Rs920m ($10.6m) and a net loss close to Rs900m.
The stores had operated under a master franchise agreement signed in 2021 between Seven & i and Reliance Retail. At its peak Reliance ran roughly 60 outlets, but the business never reached scale sufficient for branded convenience stores to be profitable amid rising competition. Quick‑commerce platforms have eroded footfall for physical convenience stores, and this makes it hard to cover rent, staffing, inventory and distribution costs. Lawson, another Japanese convenience chain, plans to open its first Mumbai outlet in 2027 and expand to 100 stores by 2030.
“We confirm that our Master Franchisee, Reliance, which operates 7-Eleven stores in Mumbai and Pune, closed all 31 stores as of 30 September 2026. We are grateful to our customers in India for their continued support,” Seven & i spokesperson said.
“While our aspiration to serve customers in India remains, we look forward to exploring several options to advance our presence in the market over the long term. At the same time, 7-Eleven International continues to strengthen its global business across existing and new markets to drive sustainable, long-term growth,” Seven & i spokesperson said.
At one time Reliance ran roughly 60 7-Eleven outlets in India, a small presence next to the rest of its retail portfolio. The spread of quick-commerce has left physical convenience stores unable to bring in enough sales to cover rent, staffing, inventory and distribution costs.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/news/7-eleven-closes-all-stores-india)

item.title: Forty senior executives weigh in on AI’s role in holiday shopping
item.description:
PYMNTS published a report based on a closed-door roundtable at Mastercard’s New York technology hub that gathered 40 senior executives to assess AI’s impact on this holiday season’s shopping. The report finds that while shoppers accept AI help for product discovery and price comparison, they remain reluctant to let software choose sellers, payment methods or finalize purchases without approval. Retailers must therefore plan for multiple tiers of AI assistance, balancing automation in routine purchases with human oversight for higher‑consideration items.
The roundtable drew leaders from retail, payments, financial services, technology and AI firms, and supplemented its discussion with PYMNTS Intelligence research on consumer and merchant attitudes.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/will-holiday-shopping-go-agentic-40-senior-execs-weigh-in)

item.title: PYMNTS launches seventh annual B2B Payments event on agentic enterprise
item.description:
PYMNTS launches its seventh annual B2B Payments event, running Oct. 5 through Oct. 14, to explore how enterprises are embedding AI into core operations. The event draws on PYMNTS Intelligence’s monthly tracking of 60 enterprise CFOs, which shows that 62% of firms now spend over $10 million on AI tools.
Three years ago, only about 30% of enterprises were fully using strategic, high‑impact generative AI, but nine months into the research 90% of CFOs reported positive returns, including in cybersecurity. PYMNTS found that while enterprises apply AI to an average of seven of eight business functions, just 20% of the 437 deployments examined are truly embedded in workflows. Among companies with three or more embedded AI functions, 93% say the technology has already paid off, compared with 25% of firms overall. Webster argues that trust and experience earned through repeated use are needed before AI can be granted authority to act autonomously within core systems.
“I think every enterprise is already agentic. And the question is how far along are they on that journey,” Karen Webster, CEO of PYMNTS said.
This year marks the seventh annual PYMNTS B2B Payments event, building on six previous editions that have examined various B2B payments trends. PYMNTS Intelligence has been tracking enterprise CFOs monthly for several years to gauge AI adoption and returns.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2026/karen-webster-says-the-agentic-enterprise-is-already-here)

item.title: Amazon’s U.S. retail spending share hits record 9.6% in September 2026
item.description:
Amazon captured 9.6% of total U.S. retail spending in the second quarter of 2026, according to a PYMNTS Intelligence report released in September. Its lead over Walmart grew to 2.09 percentage points, about twice the gap from a year earlier.
The report found Amazon gained spending share in every category tracked during the second quarter of 2026. In sporting and hobby goods, music and books, Amazon’s share was 35% compared with Walmart’s 5.1%, its largest lead across the seven categories. Electronics and appliances followed closely, with Amazon at 32.1% and Walmart at 5.3%. Amazon also led in furniture and home furnishings (9% vs 6.6%), clothing and apparel (17.8% vs 6%) and health and personal care (8% vs 7.6%). Walmart still captured 21% of food and beverage spending versus Amazon’s 3% and retained the lead in auto parts. The PYMNTS Intelligence report draws on company earnings reports and federal spending data to calculate the shares. For retailers, the findings offer a useful guide to serving shoppers: make planned purchases easy to order and give regular store visitors reasons to return.
A year earlier, Walmart held a slight advantage in health and personal care, while Amazon’s lead in furniture had grown from a small Walmart edge in 2019 to 14.3 percentage points. Overall, retail’s share of total consumer spending stabilized at 31.3%, with purchase‑prone categories rising to 24% of retail spending from 21.1% in 2019.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/amazon/2026/amazons-retail-lead-goes-beyond-electronics)

item.title: Meesho shares rise 6.1% after Jefferies retains Buy rating
item.description:
Meesho shares rose 6.1% to an intraday high of ₹240.40 on the BSE after Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating with a target price of ₹240. At 12:00 IST the stock traded 5.8% higher at ₹239.70, giving Meesho a market capitalisation of ₹1.10 lakh crore (about $11.5 billion).
Meesho’s content commerce NMV grew 152% year‑on‑year in the 12 months ended August 2026, driven by 1.6 lakh active creators, with nano creators (under 10k followers) making up 90% of the base and 81% of creators from non‑metro areas.
Meesho is also among Centrum Broking’s high‑conviction candidates for inclusion in the MSCI India Global Standard Index in its November review, as reported by Moneycontrol last month.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/meesho-shares-jump-over-6-after-jefferies-retains-buy-rating)

item.title: Honasa Consumer shares jump over 8% after upbeat Q2 FY27 outlook
item.description:
Honasa Consumer’s shares rose as much as 8.2% to ₹478.20 on the BSE in early trade after the company issued a strong business update for Q2 FY27. At 10:03 IST the stock was still 6.9% higher at ₹472.35, giving the firm a market capitalisation of roughly ₹15,368 crore.
Honasa forecast low‑thirties year‑on‑year net sales value growth for the quarter ended September 2026, with its flagship Mamaearth brand expected to deliver high‑teens growth and newer brands mid‑forties growth. The company also projects a low double‑digit operating margin, citing strong year‑on‑year improvement as it expands EBITDA margins. In the preceding quarter, consolidated net profit more than doubled to ₹90.5 crore from ₹41.3 crore, operating revenue rose 27% year‑on‑year to ₹755.9 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹110 crore from ₹46 crore. It said its distribution network now exceeds three lakh FMCG retail outlets.
The update follows Honasa’s Project Neev, which began in late 2024 to overhaul offline distribution by removing the super‑stockist layer and strengthening direct retailer servicing, and stabilised during 2025. Alongside the distribution reset, Honasa narrowed Mamaearth’s focus to five core categories—face wash, shampoo, sunscreen, moisturiser and baby care—after earlier expansion diluted execution. The firm has been building a younger brand portfolio that includes The Derma Co, Aqualogica, BBlunt, Dr Sheth’s, Staze, Lumineve and Reginald Men, and had proposed a ₹135 crore stake in nutraceuticals startup Fluence Pharma before calling off the deal in August.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/honasa-shares-jump-over-8-on-strong-q2-growth-outlook)

item.title: Adrian Cheng launches 95,000‑sqm K11 Select in Xiamen with 200 brands
item.description:
Adrian Cheng announced the launch of K11 Select in Xiamen, a 95,000‑square‑metre retail destination hosting around 200 brands. The project is positioned as a cultural tourism district that links shopping, art, urban development and wetland conservation.
Developed jointly with Xiamen Rail Transit Group, the site sits inside the Wuyuan Bay Wetland Park transit‑oriented hub. Cheng, who founded the original K11 concept in 2008, said the model aims to connect commerce, culture, city growth and natural coexistence. The opening follows Cheng’s exit from New World Development, where he stepped down as CEO in September 2024 and left the board in July 2024. Cheng’s Almad Group, created last year to manage culture, healthcare, entertainment and related ventures, oversees K11 by AC, while NWD retains its existing Hong‑Kong‑listed K11 assets.
“For me, this represents the next evolution of cultural commerce: not simply creating places to shop, but destinations that can contribute to how a city develops, how people experience culture, and how we coexist with the natural environment,” Adrian Cheng, founder of K11 said.
Prior to this, Cheng resigned from New World Development’s board and CEO role, established Almad Group to consolidate his cultural and commercial interests, and NWD continues to pursue a Shanghai C‑REIT for its own K11 properties while exploring a possible Bain Capital investment.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/10/06/adrian-cheng-takes-k11-into-xiamen-with-culture-led-retail-model)

item.title: Procuros secures €20 million Series A to expand autonomous B2B trade platform
item.description:
Hamburg-based startup Procuros recently closed a €20 million Series A funding round led by XAnge. The round brings Procuros’s total funding to date to €34 million. W23 Global joined the round as a new investor.
Procuros will use the capital to accelerate its AI‑native supply chain connectivity platform.; The funding will also support expanding its trading network internationally.; Over 300 companies are using the Procuros platform.; The platform processes more than €3 billion in annualised order volume.
“AI is advancing at incredible speed, while supply chains still run on infrastructure built decades ago. Operations teams are forced to bridge these gaps between systems that simply don’t communicate. We built Procuros to change that. Our infrastructure gives retailers, suppliers and AI agents the connectivity and trusted data they need to automate trade and make autonomous supply chains possible. Because ultimately, AI agents are only as good as the infrastructure they run on,” Patrick Thelen, CEO and Co-Founder at Procuros said.
“Procuros is showing that AI agents can make autonomous B2B trade a reality today. The team has built the infrastructure AI agents need to work across entire tradingnetworks and proven the model at scale in DACH. What excites us is the opportunity ahead: to take this beyond its home market and establish an entirely new category for global B2B trade,” Valerie Bures-Bönström, Partner and Managing Director DACH at XAnge said.
Existing backers Point Nine, Creandum, SquareOne and b2venture, which had previously backed Procuros, are participating again in this Series A.; Several angel investors are also joining the round.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/5/hamburg-based-startup-procuros-raises-20-million-series-a-for-autonomous-b2b-trade-push)

item.title: Finmid secures €17m Series A extension, total funding hits €52m
item.description:
Finmid raised €17 million in a Series A extension, lifting total funding to €52 million. The capital will fund asset‑finance products, underwriting upgrades and a first‑time move into vehicle and marketplace loans with Bolt and Skroutze.
Finmid is Berlin‑based and provides the financing technology behind Wolt, Delivery Hero and myPOS. The new €17 million round was led by Big Pi Ventures and Mainset, with Earlybird also joining the investment. The proceeds will be directed toward expanding finmid’s asset‑finance product suite. Part of the funding will upgrade the company’s multi‑source funding infrastructure. Another portion will strengthen finmid’s underwriting capabilities to support larger loan sizes. The capital also enables finmid to launch vehicle‑finance offerings for fleet operators, starting with Bolt. Additionally, the money backs marketplace‑backed loans, allowing platforms such as Skroutze to lend their own capital to merchants. This round marks finmid’s first funding event since its €23 million Series A closed in April 2024. The extension brings finmid’s total funding to date to €52 million. Investors highlight finmid’s traction in southeast Europe as evidence of untapped market opportunity. Finmid’s founders say the company’s purpose is to deliver credit that is safe, fast and regulated for any business need.
“Two years ago, embedded lending meant a cash advance for a restaurant. Today the same rails carry a multi-year vehicle loan, a marketplace's own balance sheet, and the potential for more. Every platform with business customers now has a way to become their financing partner without becoming a bank,” Alexander Talkanitsa, Co-founder said.

item.title: Morrisons appoints Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer
item.description:
Recently, Morrisons appointed Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer He will establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer
Ghasempour served as Chief AI Officer at Kingfisher from March 2024 after more than two years as Group AI Director. AI-driven personalisation increased by 16%, generating approximately £100 million in sales. Kingfisher’s marketplace GMV rose 42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales, and Screwfix Sprint 20‑minute delivery sales grew 50%.
“The creation of this new department reflects our commitment to ensuring we embrace the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus, and in the right way,” Rami Baitiéh, CEO at Morrisons said.
“Mohsen brings a phenomenal track record, joining us from Kingfisher where he built and scaled their AI operations across Europe under the leadership of my friend, Thierry Garnier,” Rami Baitiéh, CEO at Morrisons said.
Kingfisher has been using AI-enabled productivity tools such as Fabric to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion. The FTSE 100 home‑improvement retailer raised its profit target to between £595 million and £635 million, up from a previous range of £565 million to £625 million.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/5/morrisons-talks-embracing-opportunities-in-data-and-ai-as-mohsen-ghasempour-joins-grocery-retailer)

item.title: Kulczykowski joins M&S as Senior Head of Software Engineering after Maersk
item.description:
Roman Kulczykowski joined M&S as Senior Head of Software Engineering after leaving A.P. Moller - Maersk. He previously served as Technology Platform Leader and Senior Engineering Director at A.P. Moller - Maersk and was Head of SAP Technical Platforms at BP.
In his new role, he will lead teams across a broad portfolio of corporate systems, including SAP, focusing on strengthening engineering capability, improving quality and reliability, and enabling the safe and sustainable delivery of transformation. He plans to stay close to colleagues who use the technology daily, spending time with frontline teams to understand what works, identify improvements, and ensure their experience shapes technology priorities.
